blogs.title: From 4K to 2 Million Tokens: Why LongRoPE Changes What LLMs Can Remember
blogs.description: An accessible overview of the paper’s biggest headline: how LongRoPE pushes language models from typical 4K-token limits to more than 2 million tokens. The post would explain what a context window is, why it matters for tasks like document analysis, coding, agents, and long conversations, and why crossing the million-token mark is a major leap.

blogs.title: Why Long Context Is So Hard: The Hidden Positional Problem Inside LLMs
blogs.description: A beginner-friendly explanation of the core technical challenge LongRoPE solves. The post would unpack RoPE positional embeddings in plain language, show why models struggle when asked to read far beyond the positions they were trained on, and explain concepts like interpolation, crowded positions, and why performance usually collapses at extreme lengths.

blogs.title: The Smart Trick Behind LongRoPE: Searching for Better Position Encoding Instead of Rebuilding the Model
blogs.description: A post focused on LongRoPE’s main innovation: using search to find better, non-uniform ways to scale positional embeddings. It would explain how the method treats different embedding dimensions and token positions differently, why the first tokens in a sequence matter more than expected, and how an evolutionary search algorithm finds good settings without changing the model architecture.

blogs.title: How to Reach 2 Million Tokens Without Training on 2 Million-Token Documents
blogs.description: A practical explainer of LongRoPE’s progressive extension strategy. The post would show how the researchers first extend a model to 256K, fine-tune briefly, and then extend again to 2048K without needing massive long-document datasets or huge extra training runs. It would highlight why this staged approach is cheaper and more realistic than brute-force long-context training.

blogs.title: Can a 2M-Token Model Still Work on Normal Tasks? What LongRoPE’s Benchmarks Actually Show
blogs.description: A results-focused post that translates the paper’s experiments into plain English. It would cover perplexity trends, passkey retrieval performance across very long inputs, and how LongRoPE preserves short-context accuracy on standard benchmarks. The piece would help readers understand what the numbers mean in practice and where the method still shows trade-offs.
